source_text:
De xii gemmis (fragmenta ap. Anastasium Sinaitam, Quaestiones et
responsiones)
Τοῦ ἁγίουἘπιφανίου περὶ τῶν ἐν τῷ λογίῳ τοῦ ἱερέως ἐμπεπηγμένων
ιβʹ λίθων.
Σάρδιον, τὸ Βαβυλώνιον καλούμενον, πυρωπὸς μέν ἐστι καὶ αἱματώδης,
γίνεται δὲ ἐν Βαβυλῶνι τῇ πρὸςἈσσυρίους γῇ. ∆ιαυγὴς δέ ἐστι, δυνάμεως
θεραπευτικῆς, ᾧ κέχρηνται οἱ ἰατροὶ πρὸς οἰδήματα καὶ πληγὰς ἀπὸ σιδήρου
γενομένας ἀποχριόμενοι. Τοπάζιον ἐρυθρὸς μέν ἐστιν ὑπὲρ τὸν ἄνθρακα λίθον,
γίνεται δὲ ἐν Τοπάζῃ πόλει τῆςἸνδικῆς. Τριβόμενος δὲ ἐν ἰατρικῇ ἀκόνῃ, οὐκ
ἐρυθρὸν ἀποδίδωσι κατὰ τὸ χρῶμα χυμὸν, ἀλλὰ γαλακτώδη. Ἐμπίπλησι δὲ κρατῆρας
καὶ πολλοὺς, ὅσους ἂν ἐθέλῃ ὁ ὑποτρίβων, καὶ οὔτε τῷ στάθμῳ, οὔτε τῇ περιφερείᾳ
ἐλαττοῦται. Χρησιμεύει δὲ ὁ τριβόμενος ἐξ αὐτοῦ χυμὸς εἰς πάθη ὀφθαλμῶν, καὶ
πρὸς τὰς ὑδρομανίας πινόμενος, καὶ τοῖς ἀπὸ σταφυλῆς θαλασσίας μαινομένοις.
Σμάραγδος χλωρὸς μέν ἐστιν, ἐν δὲ τοῖς ὄρεσι τοῖς Ἰνδικοῖς ὀρύγοντες οἱ βάρβαροι,
κόπτουσιν αὐτόν.Ἡ δὲ δύναμις αὐτοῦ, εἰς τὸ ἐσοπτρίζεσθαι τὰ πρόσωπα. Ἄνθραξ
ὀξυφοινισσὸς μέν ἐστι τῷ εἴδει, γίνεται δὲ ἐν Καρχηδόνι τῆς Λιβύας, ἥτιςἈφρικὴ
λέγεται. Φασὶ δὲ αὐτὸν οὐκ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ, ἀλλ' ἐν νυκτὶ εὑρίσκεσθαι· πόῤῥωθεν γὰρ
δίκης λαμπάδος ἢ ἄνθρακος σπινθηρακίζων, ἐπὶ ὥραν καταπαύεται.
Ἐπιγνόντες δὲ οἱ τοῦτον ζητοῦντες, ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν, ἀπέρχονται πρὸς τὴν
αὐγὴν αὐτοῦ, καὶ εὑρίσκουσιν αὐτόν. Βασταζόμενος δὲ ὁποίοις ἂν ἱματίοις
καταλυφθῇ, ἡ αὐγὴ αὐτοῦ ἔξω τῆς παρεμβολῆς φαίνει. Σάπφειρος πορφυρίζων μέν
ἐστι, γίνεται δὲ ἐν Αἰθιοπίᾳ καὶἸνδίᾳ. Τριβόμενος δὲ, φύματα καὶ ψύδρας ἰᾶται σὺν
thought_title: The first stones of the breastplate and their powers
orientation: Epiphanius begins his description of the twelve stones set in the priest's breastplate, starting with the sardion, topazion, emerald, anthrax, and sapphire.
pass_a_gloss: Of the holy Epiphanius concerning the twelve stones fixed in the breastplate of the priest. Sardion, the one called Babylonian, is fiery-red and blood-like, and it occurs in Babylon, in the land toward the Assyrians. It is translucent, of healing power, which the doctors use for swellings and wounds that have come from iron, anointing with it. Topazion is red beyond the anthrax stone, and it occurs in Topaze, a city of India. When rubbed on a medical whetstone, it does not give back a red juice according to its color, but a milky one. It fills mixing bowls, even many, as many as the one rubbing it wishes, and it is diminished neither in weight nor in circumference. The juice rubbed from it is useful for affections of the eyes, and when drunk for water-madnesses, and for those driven mad from sea grape. Emerald is green, and the barbarians, digging in the Indian mountains, cut it. Its power is for the mirroring of faces. Anthrax is bright-red in appearance, and it occurs in Carthage of Libya, which is called Africa. Those seeking it, recognizing that this is it, go toward its gleam, and find it. When carried, with whatever garments it is wrapped, its gleam shines outside the camp. choices.english: in the breastplate of the priest
choices.why: The glossary requires 'breastplate' for λόγιον, and the genitive ἱερέως is rendered as 'of the priest' to keep the source's plain possessive.
rejected: on the oracle of the priest

choices.why: The glossary requires 'power' for δύναμις, and θεραπευτικῆς is rendered as 'healing' to preserve the adjectival force.
The glossary requires 'doctors' for ἰατροὶ, and the article is kept to match the source.
The compound is rendered literally as 'water-madnesses' to preserve the source's formation, avoiding a hyphenated compound per the instructions.
The phrase is rendered literally as 'sea grape' to preserve the source's plain wording.
The infinitive is rendered as a gerund with 'of' to keep the source's purpose construction clear and literal.

pass_b_english: From the holy Epiphanius, on the twelve stones fixed in the breastplate of the priest.

Sardion, the stone called Babylonian, is fiery-red and blood-like in appearance. It is found in Babylon, in the land toward Assyria. It is translucent and has healing power, and doctors use it by anointing with it for swellings and wounds caused by iron.

Topazion is red, more so than the anthrax stone. It is found in Topaze, a city of India. When it is rubbed on a medical whetstone, it does not yield a red juice matching its color, but a milky one. It fills mixing bowls—many of them, as many as the person rubbing it wishes—and it is not diminished either in weight or in circumference. The juice rubbed from it is useful for afflictions of the eyes, and when drunk it helps with water-madness and with those driven mad by sea-grape.
Smaragdos is green. The barbarians dig it up in the Indian mountains and cut it. Its power is for the mirroring of faces.

Anthrax is bright-red in appearance. It is found in Carthage in Libya, which is called Africa. problems.ruling: ὑδρομανίας means hydrophobia/rabies; 'water-madnesses' is nonstandard and misleading to readers.

problems.why: θαλασσίας σταφυλῆς is a plant (sea squill/Drimia maritima), not 'sea grape'
problems.ruling: θαλασσίας σταφυλῆς is sea squill (Drimia maritima), a medicinal plant, not 'sea grape'.

fixed: Changed 'water-madnesses' to 'hydrophobia' because ὑδρομανίας means hydrophobia/rabies, not 'water-madnesses'.
Changed 'sea grape' to 'sea squill' because θαλασσίας σταφυλῆς refers to the plant sea squill (Drimia maritima), not 'sea grape'.

problems.why: σταφυλὴ θαλασσία means "sea-grape," not "sea squill" (which is σκίλλα in Greek).
problems.ruling: σταφυλῆς θαλασσίας is sea-grape; sea squill is σκίλλα—wrong plant misleads cause of μαινομένοις.

problems.quote: and then after an hour it ceases
problems.why: ἐπὶ with the accusative denotes duration ("for an hour" or "for a while"), not "after an hour."
problems.ruling: ἐπὶ ὥραν is durative for an hour/a while, not temporal after an hour before καταπαύεται.

edits.old: those driven mad by sea squill
and then after an hour it ceases

fixed: sea squill -> sea-grape: fixed, source σταφυλῆς θαλασσίας is grape (not σκίλλα/squill)
after an hour -> for an hour: fixed, source ἐπὶ ὥραν καταπαύεται denotes duration of ceasing

problems.quote: and when drunk it helps with hydrophobia
problems.why: ὑδρομανίας means water-madness or morbid craving for water (dropsy), not hydrophobia (fear of water), confusing -μανία with -φοβία.
problems.fix: and when drunk it helps with water-madness
problems.ruling: ὑδρομανίας is water-madness/craving (ὕδωρ+μανία), not hydrophobia (fear of water).

edits.old: and when drunk it helps with hydrophobia
edits.new: and when drunk it helps with water-madness

fixed: hydrophobia was wrong for ὑδρομανίας (water-madness/morbid craving for water, not fear of water), fixed to water-madness

last_rejected.quote: and then after an hour it ceases
last_rejected.why: ἐπὶ ὥραν means 'at a certain hour/season', not 'after an hour'; the stone ceases glowing at a set time.
last_rejected.fix: and at a certain hour it ceases
last_rejected.ruling: ἐπὶ ὥραν can mean 'for an hour' or 'after an hour'; temporal ambiguity exists in Greek itself.

last_rejected.quote: more so than the anthrax stone
last_rejected.why: ὑπὲρ + accusative means 'above, over' in position/location, not degree of comparison; the topaz is red 'over and above' the anthrax stone in the sense of being placed above it on the breastplate, not 'more so' in color intensity.
last_rejected.fix: red, set above the anthrax stone
last_rejected.ruling: ὑπὲρ with accusative commonly means 'more than' in comparison; 'more red than the anthrax stone' is a standard rendering.

last_rejected.why: σταφυλῆς θαλασσίας refers to 'sea grape' (a poisonous marine organism causing madness), not 'sea squill' (a different plant entirely). The medical condition is from sea grape poisoning.
last_rejected.ruling: σταφυλὴ θαλασσία is sea squill (Urginea maritima), a coastal plant; LSJ supports this rendering, not 'sea grape'.

last_rejected.why: ἐσοπτρίζεσθαι is middle/passive, meaning 'to be mirrored' or 'to see one's reflection,' not active 'mirroring.' The stone's power is for faces to be reflected in it, i.e., it serves as a mirror.
last_rejected.fix: for faces to be reflected in it
last_rejected.ruling: ἐσοπτρίζεσθαι τὰ πρόσωπα means 'mirroring of faces'; the middle voice here describes the reflective function, not a mistranslation.
